modal.title: Welcome
modal.description: [p]This is an editor to manage your resume. It stores the data in portable JSON format on your local device.[/p][h5]Key Features[/h5][ul][li]The resume is stored in a single json file on your local device.[/li][li]The layout of the resume is customizable, allowing you to not only rearrange the sections to accentuate your key attributes but also to reposition the details within those sections for optimal impact.[/li][li]After crafting your resume, apply the available themes to generate HTML versions tailored for prospective employers.[/li][li]The editor supports multiple languages.[/li][/ul]

editor.title: Add Entry
editor.description: Use this button to add records to your resume. Add your work experience, education and projects.

editor.title: Action Menu
editor.description: [p]Here you can load, save and export resume, or clear the form and start over.[/p][p]Also you can select the language, change where to store your resume and change the theme.[/p]

editor.title: View your resume
editor.description: Toggle between the editor and the view mode.

editor.title: Quick Navigation and Sort Sections
editor.description: [p]Once there is data in your resume from here you can quickly scroll to the desired section.[/p][p]From here the sections could be reorders using drag and drop. Place most important sections first.[/p]

view.description: Go back to the editor from here

ai.consent_body: Pressing this button sends part of your resume to the configured AI service, where a model uses it to write a suggestion. Most buttons send only the entry you are editing, which holds none of your contact details; the profile summary sends the rest of your resume too, including your name and contact details, but never your photo. It is not retained.
ai.consent_turnstile: An automated anti-abuse check also shares your IP address and browser details with Cloudflare. Your resume is not shared with Cloudflare.
ai.pending: Generating. This can take a while...
ai.error_busy: The AI server is busy right now. Please try again in a moment.
ai.error_timeout: The AI server took too long to answer.
ai.error_failed: The AI service could not be reached.
ai.error_malformed: The AI service returned something unexpected.
ai.error_too_large: This resume is too large to send.
ai.error_turnstile: The anti-abuse check could not be loaded. AI help is unavailable for this session.
ai.disclaimer: AI can make mistakes. Read the suggestion before you use it, and check any facts, dates and figures against your own record.
ai.overwrite_warning: Using this replaces your current text and cannot be undone.
ai.busy_message: Someone else is generating right now — the server handles one request at a time. When the light turns green, press Try again.
ai.busy_hint: When the light turns green, press Try again.
waiting: Don't lean on AI too hard — you know your own work best.
Working out what this is all about...
Assembling plausible-sounding sentences...
A good line says what you did, not what you were responsible for.
Numbers beat adjectives. Add a figure where you can.
Reading between your bullet points...
Tailor this to the job you actually want.
Whatever comes back is a first draft, never a final one.
Consulting the collected wisdom of the internet. Mixed results.
Recruiters skim. Put the strongest thing first.
Thinking. Slowly, but thinking.
If a sentence could describe anyone, it describes no one.
Warming up the language model...
Your own words are usually better. Treat this as a nudge.
Trimming the corporate filler...
'Synergy' has never got anyone hired.
Looking for verbs that mean something...
The best line on a resume is one only you could have written.
Still going. Small models take their time.
Checking whether that really needed three sentences.
Hunting for the achievement hiding in the job description...
Every claim here is yours to verify.
Rearranging words until they sound confident...
A model can phrase it. Only you know whether it is true.
Looking for the part a hiring manager would care about...
Turning duties into accomplishments...
Fact-checking is still your job.
Almost there. Probably.
